quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #24
										  					
  

25 Questions • Passing Score 18

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Steep downgrade ahead.
Crossroad ahead.
No right turn.
Narrow bridge.

questions.correctAnswerText: Steep downgrade ahead.
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black markings. They tell drivers about hazards ahead. This sign warns you about a steep hill coming up. Slow down to protect your brakes and avoid a crash.

questions.question: You must pull over and let an emergency vehicle pass:

options.text: No matter which direction it is coming from.
Only if it is behind you.
Only if it is coming toward you.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: No matter which direction it is coming from.
questions.explanation: Pull over to the right edge and stop for any emergency vehicle with flashing lights. Do this whether it is behind you or coming from the opposite direction.

questions.question: When you see a flashing yellow arrow at a traffic light, you should:

options.text: Move into the lane the arrow points to.
Come to a complete stop.
Turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.
Turn without worrying about oncoming traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left after letting oncoming traffic and pedestrians go first.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow arrow means you can turn left in that direction. But oncoming traffic has a green light. You must yield to them and to pedestrians before you turn.

questions.question: Green pavement on the road means:

options.text: Emergency lanes.
An area where cars and bicycles may conflict.
HOV lanes.
An eco-friendly area.

questions.correctAnswerText: An area where cars and bicycles may conflict.
questions.explanation: Green pavement marks areas where cars and bicycles share the road. Watch carefully for cyclists. Do not stop on green pavement at a red light.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No U-turn.
No turning.
No left turn.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign says you cannot make a U-turn. Do not turn around at this location.

questions.question: In bad weather, drivers should:

options.text: Drive faster to get to their destination quickly.
Follow other cars more closely.
Stay farther away from the car in front.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther away from the car in front.
questions.explanation: On wet roads, increase the distance between your car and the car ahead of you.

questions.question: Before driving to a new place, you should:

options.text: Just follow road signs to find your way.
Plan your trip before you drive.
Only know the general area where you are going.
Always choose the shortest route.

questions.correctAnswerText: Plan your trip before you drive.
questions.explanation: Always plan your trip in advance before driving to an unfamiliar place. Check a map before you start. Don't begin your trip without knowing where you are going.

questions.question: If a car is coming straight at you in your lane, you should:

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and slow down.
Honk, steer right, and slow down.
Stay centered, honk, and slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and slow down.
questions.explanation: First, honk your horn to get the other driver's attention. If they don't move, steer to the right. Don't steer left because they might correct at the last second and you will still crash. Brake firmly and steadily. Every mile per hour you lose reduces the impact.

questions.question: Your car takes longer to stop when stopping on:

options.text: Wet or icy roads.
Paved highways.
When driving at night.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wet or icy roads.
questions.explanation: Stopping distance is longer on wet or icy roads. It also increases on loose gravel or stones.

questions.question: You hear a siren but cannot see the emergency vehicle. What should you do?

options.text: Keep driving until you see it.
Pull to the side and look to see if it is on your street.
Slow down but don't stop.
Speed up and turn at the next corner.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull to the side and look to see if it is on your street.
questions.explanation: If you hear a siren close by but don't know where the emergency vehicle is, safely pull to the right side and stop. Wait until you are sure it is not heading toward you.

questions.question: On a road with no sidewalk, where should a pedestrian walk?

options.text: On the side with the lightest traffic.
On the same side where traffic is moving.
On the side facing oncoming traffic.
On the side with the heaviest traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the side facing oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: Walk on the side of the road where you can see cars coming toward you.

questions.question: What should you do when approaching an intersection with no traffic signals or stop signs?

options.text: Keep driving at the same speed.
Stop completely, look both ways, and then go.
Let all other drivers go first.
Be ready to yield to other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to yield to other cars.
questions.explanation: Be prepared to yield at uncontrolled intersections. Slow down, cover your brake, and look left, right, and left again. Yield to any car coming from the right.

questions.question: Your car is in an accident and is blocking traffic. What should you do?

options.text: Move your car off the road if you can.
Do not move your car at all.
Wait for police to arrive before moving your car.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move your car off the road if you can.
questions.explanation: After a minor accident, move your car out of traffic if possible. Always stay at the scene and tell the other people who you are.

questions.question: What is true about a work zone?

options.text: It can be moving or staying in one place.
It is marked with black and white signs.
You do not need to slow down or pay attention.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can be moving or staying in one place.
questions.explanation: Work zones can be stationary or moving (like vehicles mowing or removing snow). They are marked with orange signs. Always slow down and pay attention in work zones.

questions.question: When parking downhill on a two-way street, which way should you turn your wheels?

options.text: Turn them to the right.
Turn them to the left.
Keep them pointed straight.
Leave the transmission in neutral.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn them to the right.
questions.explanation: Turn your wheels toward the side of the road. If your car rolls downhill, it will roll away from traffic.

questions.question: What traffic light means: stop completely, yield to other traffic and people, then go when it is safe?

options.text: A solid red light.
A flashing yellow light.
A solid green light.
A flashing red light.

questions.correctAnswerText: A flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. Stop completely, yield to other cars and people walking, then go when it is safe.

questions.question: What can a leaking exhaust system cause?

options.text: Your car uses too much oil.
Your car needs a tune-up sooner.
You feel sleepy while driving.
Grass fires start on country roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: You feel sleepy while driving.
questions.explanation: A leaky exhaust system releases toxic gases. These fumes can make you very drowsy while driving and are dangerous.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Sharp turn to the right.
Double curve.
Road with many curves ahead.
Pavement ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road with many curves ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road ahead has a series of curves.

questions.question: When you see a solid yellow light at a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon, what must you do?

options.text: Go forward carefully.
Stop completely, then go carefully.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
Stop and wait for a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light at a Pedestrian Hybrid Beacon means slow down and prepare to stop. This beacon helps people safely cross the road.

questions.question: On a highway outside of towns and business areas, what is the speed limit if no sign says otherwise?

options.text: 10 mph.
20 mph.
30 mph.
50 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: 50 mph.
questions.explanation: Unless a sign shows a different speed limit, do not drive faster than 50 mph on highways outside of towns and business areas.

questions.question: If a green arrow changes to a solid green light, what should you do?

options.text: You can still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
You can no longer turn and must go straight.
You still have the right to turn.
You no longer need to turn in the direction the arrow pointed.

questions.correctAnswerText: You can still turn, but you must let oncoming traffic go first.
questions.explanation: When a green arrow changes to a solid green light, you can still turn in that direction. But first, you must yield to pedestrians and oncoming traffic.

questions.question: What does a single broken white line in the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in opposite directions and passing is allowed when safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is not allowed.
Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in the same direction and passing is allowed when safe.
questions.explanation: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction. Broken lines mean you can pass when it is safe to do so.

questions.question: What color are signs for public recreation areas?

options.text: Orange
Red
Green
Brown

questions.correctAnswerText: Brown
questions.explanation: Brown signs mark public recreation areas and places of historical or cultural interest. They help you find these locations when you are traveling.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line mean?

options.text: Passing is allowed from both directions.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
Passing is allowed from the lane with the solid line.
Passing is not allowed from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Passing is allowed from the lane with the broken line.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line next to a solid yellow line means you can pass only from the side with the broken line.

questions.question: What is a speed limit?

options.text: The fastest or slowest legal speed on a road in dangerous conditions.
The fastest or slowest legal speed on a road in good conditions.
The suggested speed for a road in good conditions.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest or slowest legal speed on a road in good conditions.
questions.explanation: A speed limit is the fastest or slowest legal speed you can drive in good conditions. You can drive slower than the limit, but not faster. Drive slower in school zones, work zones, or when conditions like construction or bad weather make it unsafe.
